chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from his father, who said:
I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the reason for which the woman divorced by ṭalāq al-ʿiddah does not become lawful again for her husband "until she marries another husband."
So he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has only permitted divorce twice, and the Mighty and Majestic said:
Divorce is twice; then keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.

Meaning in the third pronouncement of divorce: because he entered into that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disliked for him of the third divorce, He made her unlawful for him, so she is not lawful for him "until she marries another husband."
This is so that people may not treat divorce lightly and may not harm women."

key_terms.الِاسْتِخْفَافَ بِالطَّلَاقِ: treating divorce lightly or with disregard
key_terms.الْعِلَّةِ: the underlying reason or legal rationale for the ruling
key_terms.لِلْعِدَّةِ: in the context of a revocable divorce tied to the waiting period
key_terms.مَرَّتَيْنِ: twice, indicating the limit mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Why does a woman divorced three times not become lawful for her husband until she marries another husband?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that after a third divorce, the woman does not become lawful again for her former husband until she marries another husband, because Allah has permitted divorce only twice before this final consequence takes effect. The ruling serves as a deterrent against making light of divorce and protects women from being harmed through repeated and careless repudiation.
